blocks.raw: <Tip>**Utility Memory Aids:** Water = pressure + storage if needed. Sewage = 1% slope minimum (never flat). Stormwater = 2% slope or retention. Electrical = separated above wet utilities. Easements = PD 1067 (river 26m), road (6–10m), utilities (3–5m). These reduce buildable area; account early in site planning.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Ignoring sewage slope requirements; assuming flat pipes will work (causes backups and failures)","Underestimating water demand or storage; many Philippine sites require elevated tanks because municipal pressure is inconsistent","Locating utilities in building footprints or landscape zones; always reserve easement first","Failing to coordinate with municipal authorities early; utility upgrades delay projects by months or years","Treating stormwater as secondary; inadequate drainage causes flooding and foundation damage","Overlooking secondary easements (gas, telecommunications); these consume land even if not immediately needed","Routing electrical above sewage or water; cross-contamination risk if lines fail","Forgetting that green infrastructure (BERDE) requires larger easement for bioretention basins or wetlands"]} />
